title: Create True-Shape Links
subtitle: Redissolving candidate centerlines and splitting only at snapped model nodes to produce true-shape link pieces
description: CandidateTDMRoadLinks is fully re-dissolved into maximal topological chains per VERT_LEVEL (undoing incidental arcpy junction cuts), then split only at snapped WFRC model-node and CC-attachment positions to produce the raw building-block pieces for true-shape link conflation. Lineage/display attributes (OBJECTID, UNIQUE_ID, DOT_FCLASS, etc.) are reattached onto each piece via a midpoint-nearest join against CandidateTDMRoadLinks.

## Setup

### Imports

::: {#3106d6e7 .cell execution_count=1}

``` {.python .cell-code}
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from shapely.geometry import Point

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path.cwd()))
from _src.link_utils import resolve_snap_coords, split_candidate_links
from _src.centerline_utils import dissolve_and_singlepart, transfer_attributes_by_midpoint
```
:::


### Configuration

::: {#664e7627 .cell execution_count=2}
``` {.python .cell-code}

    "in_node_snapped": Path("_data/processed/nodes_snapped.gpkg"),
    "out_link_pieces": Path("_data/processed/link_pieces.gpkg"),
}

# Lineage/display attributes reattached onto final pieces via midpoint join
# (see Part D) — same column list 00_data_preparation.qmd uses for the
# original CandidateTDMRoadLinks midpoint transfer.
TRANSFER_COLS = [
    "OBJECTID",
    "UNIQUE_ID",
    "DOT_FCLASS",
    "POSTTYPE",
    "DOT_RTNAME",
    "DOT_HWYNAM",
    "FULLNAME",
    "CARTOCODE",
    "ONEWAY",
    "VERT_LEVEL",
    "SPEED_LMT",
]

# ── CRS ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
CRS_UTM = "EPSG:26912"  # NAD83 UTM Zone 12N — Utah (metric)
```

## Load Data

### Candidate Centerlines

`CandidateTDMRoadLinks.gpkg` (built in `00_data_preparation.qmd`) is already
filtered and dissolved, but it is also pre-cut at arcpy-style junction
points — including incidental boundaries between freeway/ramp/CD rows and
surface-street rows wherever they merely touch, not just at genuine
multi-way branches. Part A below re-dissolves these rows into maximal
chains so that every split point in the final pieces (Part C) comes only
from snapping, not from `CandidateTDMRoadLinks`'s own pre-existing cuts.

::: {#9bf8eade .cell execution_count=3}
``` {.python .cell-code}
gdf_centerlines = gpd.read_file(PATHS["in_centerlines"]).to_crs(CRS_UTM)

print(f"Candidate components: {len(gdf_centerlines):,} | CRS: {gdf_centerlines.crs}")
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}
```
Candidate components: 7,642 | CRS: EPSG:26912
```
:::
:::

::: {#dfe48873 .cell execution_count=4}

``` {.python .cell-code}
gdf_cc_snapped    = gpd.read_file(PATHS["in_node_snapped"], layer="cc_nodes_snapped").to_crs(CRS_UTM)

n_snapped = gdf_nodes_snapped["snapped"].fillna(False).sum()
print(f"Nodes: {n_total:,} total | {n_snapped:,} snapped ({n_snapped/n_total:.1%})")
print(f"CC attachment nodes: {len(gdf_cc_snapped):,}")
```

---

## Part A — Full Network Redissolve

`CandidateTDMRoadLinks` is already pre-cut at arcpy-style junction points
(see `00_data_preparation.qmd`'s `rcl_merge`), including boundaries between
freeway/ramp/CD rows and surface-street rows wherever they merely touch —
not just at genuine multi-way branches. To make the final true-shape split
points come **only** from snapped model nodes, every row is re-dissolved
into maximal topological chains first, per `VERT_LEVEL` (freeway and
surface rows combined within a level — genuine branch points, where 3+
lines share an endpoint, still remain hard boundaries after dissolve;
only incidental class-boundary splits are undone).

VERT_LEVEL isolation is preserved deliberately: dissolving across levels
would incorrectly fuse an elevated/tunnel structure with an at-grade road
sharing the same XY footprint (see `dissolve_and_singlepart` docstring).

::: {#74c7e6cb .cell execution_count=6}
``` {.python .cell-code}
vert_levels = sorted(gdf_centerlines["VERT_LEVEL"].dropna().unique())
print(f"VERT_LEVELs present: {vert_levels}")

fulldissolve_parts = []
for lvl in vert_levels:
    subset = gdf_centerlines[gdf_centerlines["VERT_LEVEL"] == lvl]
    if subset.empty:
        continue
    dissolved = dissolve_and_singlepart(subset)
    print(f"  VERT_LEVEL {lvl}: {len(subset):,} rows -> {len(dissolved):,} dissolved chains")
    fulldissolve_parts.append(dissolved)

gdf_fulldissolve = gpd.GeoDataFrame(
    pd.concat(fulldissolve_parts, ignore_index=True),
    geometry="geometry",
    crs=gdf_centerlines.crs,
)
print(f"\nTotal: {len(gdf_centerlines):,} candidate rows -> {len(gdf_fulldissolve):,} redissolved chains")
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}
```
VERT_LEVELs present: ['0', '1', '2', '3']
  VERT_LEVEL 0: 6,940 rows -> 6,586 dissolved chains
  VERT_LEVEL 1: 669 rows -> 526 dissolved chains
  VERT_LEVEL 2: 28 rows -> 25 dissolved chains
  VERT_LEVEL 3: 5 rows -> 4 dissolved chains

Total: 7,642 candidate rows -> 7,141 redissolved chains
```
:::
:::


Sanity check: dissolve only merges touching lines into longer chains — it
never adds or removes length. Total length before and after must match.

::: {#2e7d9efa .cell execution_count=7}
``` {.python .cell-code}
len_before = gdf_centerlines.geometry.length.sum()
len_after = gdf_fulldissolve.geometry.length.sum()
diff_m = abs(len_before - len_after)
print(f"Total length before: {len_before:,.1f} m")
print(f"Total length after:  {len_after:,.1f} m")
print(f"Difference:          {diff_m:.3f} m")
assert diff_m < 1.0, "Redissolve changed total network length — investigate before proceeding."
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}
```
Total length before: 6,424,286.6 m
Total length after:  6,424,286.6 m
Difference:          0.000 m
```
:::
:::

## Part B — Resolve Snap Coordinates

`nodes_snapped.gpkg` stores `snapped_x_round / snapped_y_round` rounded to 2 decimal
places (cm precision). Splitting and M-value operations require coordinates that
exactly match a vertex stored in the centerline geometry. For each snapped node,
this step finds the nearest unique centerline vertex within 5 cm and records its
full-precision coordinate.

FixedTransit_Rail nodes are excluded — they snap to GTFS rail infrastructure
(CRT stations, LRT midpoints), not to road centerlines, so they are never road
centerline split points.

::: {#28de25c1 .cell execution_count=8}
``` {.python .cell-code}
gdf_nodes_road = gdf_nodes_snapped[
    gdf_nodes_snapped["snap_rule"] != "FixedTransit_Rail"
]
gdf_nodes_resolved = resolve_snap_coords(
    gdf_nodes_road,
    gdf_fulldissolve,
    tolerance=0.05,
)

n_road_snapped = gdf_nodes_road["snapped"].fillna(False).sum()
n_resolved     = gdf_nodes_resolved["snap_resolved"].sum()
n_unresolved   = n_road_snapped - n_resolved
print(f"Coordinate resolution: {n_resolved:,} resolved | {n_unresolved:,} unresolved")
```

Build the list of exact-coordinate Points used as split locations.

::: {#796cedda .cell execution_count=10}

``` {.python .cell-code}
resolved_mask = gdf_nodes_resolved["snap_resolved"]
snap_points_exact = [
    Point(row["x_exact"], row["y_exact"])
    for _, row in gdf_nodes_resolved[resolved_mask].iterrows()
]
print(f"Split points prepared: {len(snap_points_exact):,}")
```

## Part C — Split at Snapped Nodes

`gdf_fulldissolve` (Part A) — not the original `CandidateTDMRoadLinks` rows —
is split at every model-node snap point and every CC attachment snap point,
so piece boundaries come only from snapping, never from incidental
arcpy junction cuts. Points that project to within 0.1 mm of a component's
existing endpoint are skipped (already a boundary). After all splits, each
resulting piece is bounded exclusively by:
- a snapped model node position,
- a snapped CC attachment node position, or
- a genuine branch point already present in `gdf_fulldissolve`.

No lineage keys are carried through this split (`id_cols=()`) — a redissolved
row no longer maps 1:1 to a single original `OBJECTID`. Lineage/display
attributes are reattached afterward via midpoint join (Part D).

::: {#5c69360c .cell execution_count=11}
``` {.python .cell-code}
cc_resolved = gdf_cc_snapped[gdf_cc_snapped["snap_resolved"]]
cc_snap_points = [
    Point(row["x_snap"], row["y_snap"])
    for _, row in cc_resolved.iterrows()
]
all_snap_points = snap_points_exact + cc_snap_points
n_cc_unresolved = len(gdf_cc_snapped) - len(cc_resolved)
print(
    f"Split points: {len(snap_points_exact):,} (model nodes) + "
    f"{len(cc_snap_points):,} (CC attachment, {n_cc_unresolved:,} unresolved excluded) "
    f"= {len(all_snap_points):,} total"
)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}
```
Split points: 3,598 (model nodes) + 5,948 (CC attachment, 591 unresolved excluded) = 9,546 total
```
:::
:::


::: {#2faa8a47 .cell execution_count=12}
``` {.python .cell-code}
print(f"Splitting {len(gdf_fulldissolve):,} redissolved chains at {len(all_snap_points):,} points …")
gdf_pieces_split = split_candidate_links(gdf_fulldissolve, all_snap_points, id_cols=())
print(f"Pieces after split: {len(gdf_pieces_split):,}")
```

## Part D — Build Pieces Layer, Reattach Lineage, and Export

Extract start/end endpoint coordinates for each piece (rounded to 2 dp for
matching against `snapped_x_round / snapped_y_round` in the next stage). Since
splitting now runs against the redissolved `gdf_fulldissolve` layer, a piece
no longer maps 1:1 to a single original `CandidateTDMRoadLinks` `OBJECTID` —
lineage/display attributes (`TRANSFER_COLS`) are reattached via the same
midpoint-nearest-join approach `00_data_preparation.qmd` uses to transfer
attributes from raw centerlines onto `CandidateTDMRoadLinks` in the first
place, this time from `CandidateTDMRoadLinks` onto each piece.

::: {#4ab436bf .cell execution_count=13}
``` {.python .cell-code}
pieces = gdf_pieces_split.geometry.tolist()
start_coords = np.array([p.coords[0] for p in pieces])
end_coords   = np.array([p.coords[-1] for p in pieces])

gdf_pieces = gpd.GeoDataFrame(
    {
        "piece_id": np.arange(len(pieces)),
        "x_start":  np.round(start_coords[:, 0], 2),
        "y_start":  np.round(start_coords[:, 1], 2),
        "x_end":    np.round(end_coords[:, 0], 2),
        "y_end":    np.round(end_coords[:, 1], 2),
        "length_m": np.array([p.length for p in pieces]),
        "geometry": pieces,
    },
    crs=CRS_UTM,
)

gdf_pieces = transfer_attributes_by_midpoint(gdf_pieces, gdf_centerlines, TRANSFER_COLS)

n_null = gdf_pieces[TRANSFER_COLS].isna().any(axis=1).sum()
print(f"Pieces with a null transferred attribute: {n_null:,} / {len(gdf_pieces):,}")

PATHS["out_link_pieces"].parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
gdf_pieces.to_file(PATHS["out_link_pieces"], driver="GPKG")
print(f"Exported {len(gdf_pieces):,} pieces → {PATHS['out_link_pieces']}")
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}
```

Exported 12,253 pieces → _data\processed\link_pieces.gpkg
```
:::
